text: When you work with APIs, you send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use in your code. Before making requests, you often need authentication, usually by including an API key or token in your request header. But be careful—many APIs have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests per minute. If you exceed them, you’ll get an error. That’s why good error handling is essential: you should always check the response status and write code to handle problems, like retrying after a short wait or showing a friendly message.
